observed_facts.envelope_required_in_same_result_commit: validation_rules[0]: 'envelope is committed BY THE LEAF at the frozen owned path in the SAME result commit'
observed_facts.verifier_compares_envelope_result_tree_s: acceptance-verifier-v3.1.py check_envelope: head_tree = run([git, -C, checkout, rev-parse, 'HEAD^{tree}']); 'result_tree_sha_matches': env.get('result_tree_sha') == head_tree
observed_facts.envelope_blob_is_an_input_of_head_tree: the envelope is committed at the frozen owned path (receipts/headless-lab-results-v3.1/<lab>-result.json) inside the result commit; its blob is therefore a component of the result commit tree, so the tree OID that the envelope declares depends on the envelope's own bytes

semantics.schema_labels_result_tree_sha_as_sha256: required_fields.result_tree_sha: 'SHA-256 of the result commit tree (resolved externally as HEAD^{tree})'
semantics.verifier_obtains_git_object_id_via_rev_p: git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} returns a Git object ID (SHA-1 in sha1 object format), not a file SHA-256

classification.note: Writing the envelope changes the tree OID the envelope is required to declare. A correct same-commit envelope would require the tree OID to be a fixed point of the commit-with-envelope mapping; no claim is made that such a fixed point is absolutely impossible, only that it is not constructible by the ordinary git workflow and would require a cryptographic fixed point.

attribution.note: This is a structural/semantic defect of the v3.1 envelope model, reproduced from exact tracked bytes. The v3.1 exact-byte review (CP-057) remains valid HISTORICAL evidence for the bytes reviewed.
